name: Braided Estuary
desc: A braided river reaching the sea, seen straight down from altitude — anastomosing threads wander and rejoin across a bright gravel corridor, old paleochannel scars cut the floodplain where the river used to run, sediment plumes bloom out of every distributary mouth and lean with the tide, and a cloud deck drifts across offset from its own shadow on the ground; true-colour satellite, 4-3-2 false colour, a bathymetric chart, a peat-stained tannin estuary, or a glacial outwash sandur.

energy.doc: how hard the scene burns — plume opacity, specular glint on the water and overall contrast

scale.doc: altitude — big scale zooms in to few wide channels, small pulls back to a fine braid (rebuilds the ground)

density.doc: how many threads braid the corridor, plus paleochannel and glint count

silt.doc: sediment load — how far the plumes reach into the sea

cloud.doc: cloud-deck cover and how dark its shadows fall on the ground

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default ochre-sediment / dark-water pairing

x.doc: where the braid corridor runs across the frame

y.doc: the shoreline — how much frame is land versus open water

style.doc: aesthetic: landsat = true-colour satellite pass, ochre sediment and muted floodplain; falsecolor = 4-3-2 false colour, living vegetation burns red and water goes navy void; bathy = bathymetric chart, depth-banded ramp and spot soundings, no land texture; tannin = peat-stained estuary under low cloud, near-monochrome and moody; ice = glacial outwash sandur, grey silt, black sand, milk-blue meltwater

act.doc: multi-minute tide programme — plumes push out on the ebb, fold back on the flood, or run brown in spate

seed.doc: regenerates the braid, the paleochannels and the cloud deck

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
